decision_lens: Prioritizes findings that would explain the 6.6 ceiling as an evaluation artifact rather than genuine model quality ceiling — a flawed ruler cannot guide improvement.
focus: Whether the LLM-as-judge evaluation can detect a 0.4-point improvement and whether 6.6 accurately reflects reconstruction quality or measurement artifacts
name: fd-eval-blind-spots
persona: A psychometrician who has audited NLP evaluation rubrics for construct validity and sensitivity. Treats every aggregate score as a hypothesis that must be stress-tested.
review_areas: Audit curated evaluator panel composition: if all GPT-family, they may share biases blind to GPT-5.4 failure modes
Check whether rubric dimensions are sensitive to 6.6 vs 7.0 quality difference — coarse anchors may have resolution floor above 0.4
Verify whether judge prompt provides constitution and CIPHER to evaluator — without them judge cannot distinguish principled deviation from error
Assess whether LLM judges show position bias by checking if eval code randomizes ordering
Check whether per-pillar scores correlate with human accept/reject decisions
Examine scoring scale (1-10 vs 1-5) and composite aggregation for mixed-scale issues
success_hints: 0.4-point target must exceed measurement noise floor — verify via inter-evaluator standard deviation
Human editorial accept/reject rates should correlate (Spearman r > 0.5) with composite scores
If all curated evaluators are same family as reconstructor, self-evaluation bias is confounded
task_context: The system extracts constitution via Inverse CAI and CIPHER preferences from professional before/after pairs. GPT-5.4 scores 6.6/10 and prompt engineering hit a ceiling.
